summary: Shujiro Shimada (1907–1994) worked in Japanology, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University circa 1928–1931 and held a position at Princeton University from around 1962 to 1975.

Shujun Motegi is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Banaras Hindu University under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi and earned an MA from Kyoto University in 1977, later serving as Professor of Ethics at Shinshu University (attested 1998, 2010).

Shuken Ito (born 1947) specializes in Buddhist studies. He completed undergraduate through doctoral studies at Komazawa University, subsequently serving there as research assistant, lecturer, associate professor, and professor between 1970 and 1991, and as visiting professor at Aichi Gakuin University in 1998.

Shuman Chen works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Chen completed a PhD at Northwestern University under doctoral supervisor Brook Ziporyn and also studied under traditional teacher Weijue Shi.

Shuming Liang (1893–1988) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. Educated at Shuntian Middle School (circa 1906–1911), he joined the philosophy department at Peking University in 1917 and founded the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute and China Democratic League.

Shumpei Ueyama (1921–2012) was a philosophy and Japanology scholar who studied at Taihoku High School and Kyoto University. He taught at Kyoto University (1954–1984), later serving as Director of Kyoto National Museum (~1986–1994) and President of Kyoto City University of Arts (~1989–1995).
Shun Hidaka works in Buddhist studies. Hidaka served as a researcher at the Buddhist Art Resource Center in 2012 and as a part-time lecturer at Otani University (attested 2014).

Shun'ei Hirai (born 1930) is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. At Komazawa University, he served as lecturer, professor, vice president, and emeritus professor between 1964 and 2001.
Shunei Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. Mori held a post as a part-time lecturer at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College (attested 1995).
Shunei Tsuboi (1923–2010) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Bukkyo University (attested 1963 and 1972).

Shunji Hosaka (born 1956) works in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Waseda University (circa 1975–1979), he held positions at Reitaku University, Chuo University, the Eastern Institute, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and IIBS.

Shunkyo Katsumata (1909–1994) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1932–1935). He held positions at Toyo University and Taisho University, where he served from around 1957 to 1980 as professor and emeritus professor.

Shunryu Suzuki (1904–1971) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and Eihei-ji under several traditional teachers. He served as abbot at Zoun-in, Rinsō-in, and Sōkō-ji, and founded the San Francisco Zen Center and Tassajara.

Shunsho Manabe (1939–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Tohoku University (circa 1960–1968) and held posts at Hosen Gakuen College and Shikoku University, where he was a professor circa 1999–2010.
Shunsho Terakawa (1928–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held a post at Otani University from circa 1964 to 2000, where he became emeritus professor.
Shuntaro Kondo is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Ryukoku University in 2011 and served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2012).

Shuntaro Matsuyama (1930–2014) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, later lecturing at Bigakko, Kokugakuin University, and Tama Art University, and serving as professor at Joshibi University of Art and Design (~1988–1996).

Shunzo Onoda specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a D.Lit. at Bukkyo University in 1993, where he later served as associate professor (attested 1996) and professor (attested 2005).

Shuyu Kanaoka (1927–2009) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and earned a doctorate from Toyo University in 1962. He served as an associate professor at Toyo University from circa 1966 to 1992.

Shuyu Sakurai (born 1916) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University from circa 1940 to 1943. He held a post at Komazawa University from around 1956 to 1987, where he became emeritus professor.
